function: Learned generation of multipath AoA/AoD angles, LoS status and number of paths from UE and BS locations, used as channel support for LS channel estimation (pp. 6-7).
system: Hybrid OFDM mmWave massive MIMO, BS 8x4 UPA (32 antennas), UE 4x2 UPA (8), 60 GHz, 50 MHz, 512 subcarriers; no RIS (pp. 5, 12-13).
method: Supervised conditional generative learning: two MLP classifiers (LoS status, number of paths) and per-path conditional GANs with residual 1D-CNN generator/discriminator, reconstruction plus adversarial loss, then classical LS (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: DeepMIMO O1 ray-tracing scenario at 60 GHz, User Grid 1, 18 BSs, 8,962,758 samples, Lp=4 strongest paths; random 80/10/10 split; Boston5G for second map (pp. 12-14, 20).
test_conditions: Random 80/10/10 split of O1 (p. 14); SNR -20 to 20 dB, 20-120 pilots, UE position errors 0.5-3 m (pp. 16-17); spatial block hold-out (p. 19); Boston5G map (p. 20).
baselines: Non-learned: SW-OMP (compressive sensing, two grids), oversampled-DFT codebook, perfect-CSI SVD bound, CRLB. Learned: tailored conditional DDPM (pp. 12, 16-19).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, pilots, RF chains, antennas; spectral efficiency; LoS/NoP classification accuracy (99.96%/99.52%); angular accuracy within 1 degree, MAAE, RMSAE; run time (pp. 14-19).
complexity: Online complexity O(KMLp + MLp^2 + Lp^3) versus SW-OMP O(K Gr Gt M Lr L); runtime 0.148 ms (CG-CGAN), 0.228 ms (DDPM), 819.4 ms (SW-OMP) (pp. 11-12, 19).
openness: Code and instructions released at https://github.com/yildirimbk/CG-CGAN-Angle-Generation-and-Channel-Estimation-Framework (p. 3, footnote 2); public DeepMIMO dataset used.
q1_support: p. 12: "from the DeepMIMO dataset [58], [73], configured at a 60 GHz operating frequency" and "generated via ray-tracing simulations in Wireless InSite". DeepMIMO ray tracing is a listed standard source.
q2_support: p. 14: "The dataset is randomly split into 80% for training, 10% for validation, and 10% for testing". p. 19: "we introduce a region-based spatial split of the dataset" holds out blocks of the same O1 map. p. 20: "it inherently operates as a site-specific model", so Boston5G is a new training site and no fine-tuning from O1 is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "We benchmark its performance against the SW-OMP method [25] and a tailored conditional DDPM [57], [72]". SW-OMP is non-learned; the DDPM is a standard generative model applied to the same angle-generation problem. Figs. 7-10 compare NMSE and spectral efficiency (pp. 16-19).
q4_support: p. 12: "the overall online complexity of the CG-CGAN-based CE is upper bounded by" O(K M Lp + M Lp^2 + Lp^3) (Table 3, p. 11); p. 19: Table 11 lists run time 0.148 ms (CG-CGAN), 0.228 ms (DDPM), 819.4 ms (SW-OMP).
q5_support: p. 3: "The code and instructions to reproduce our results is available at" https://github.com/yildirimbk/CG-CGAN-Angle-Generation-and-Channel-Estimation-Framework (footnote 2); p. 12: trained and tested on the DeepMIMO O1 scenario.
notes: Include, area 2: the learned classifiers and per-path CGANs take BS/UE positions and generate AoA/AoD, while path gains come from classical LS with pilots (pp. 6-7). q2 borderline, marked 0: the unseen-block split (p. 19-20) is a hold-out of the same O1 data, Boston5G uses a site-specific model that is trained on that map, and Section VI-G announces transfer learning (p. 19) but reports no fine-tuning; if the reviewer accepts the unseen-block test as a new site, q2 becomes 1. Sweeps of antennas, pilots and RF chains change only the LS stage, since the learned models use positions only (p. 7). Tables 3-9 and 11 were read from page images. A conference version [55] exists; only this journal version was graded.
